articles.title: Quentin Tarantino Says He's 'Written a Script' for 10th and Final Film, But He Wants to 'Live' Before Making It
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino has confirmed he's "written a script" for his 10th and final film, but he's going to "live" a little before making it. The Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood and Kill Bill filmmaker teased his plans for his long-in-development finale movie during an appearance on The Graham Norton…
body: "I've written a script that I could do that I really, really like, but I have to do the play and see who I am, right?" Tarantino said, referencing his upcoming West End play, The Popinjay Cavalier.
"I'll finish the play, and then I'll go back, be with my family for a while, and then live and then see what that guy wants to do."

The director's words were in response to a question from show host Graham Norton, who asked about his "10th" and "final film." Tarantino didn't skip a beat when conjuring up his reply, suggesting that, yes, the plan is still for his next film to be his last whenever it does eventually hit screens.

For reference, The Popinjay Cavalier is set to start previews February 23, 2027, and then open one month later, March 18. That means we've got some waiting to do before Tarantino will begin the "then live" phase of his pre-movie plan. How long it will be before he then decides on a script, begins production, and settles on a release date remains to be seen, but don't expect to hear any significant updates for a while.
points: Quentin Tarantino has confirmed he's "written a script" for his 10th and final film, but he's going to "live" a little before making it.
"I've written a script that I could do that I really, really like, but I have to do the play and see who I am, right?
"I'll finish the play, and then I'll go back, be with my family for a while, and then live and then see what that guy wants to do."

articles.title: 36 Years Later, Robert De Niro's Greatest Gangster Movie Quote Is Still One of a Kind
articles.summary: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro. Across decades of mob dramas, he's played men who command respect through intimidation, calculation, and a religious devotion to the rules of their world.
body: Through all these roles, De Niro has delivered plenty of unforgettable lines, but one of his most memorable isn't a threat or a declaration of power. It's a deceptively simple piece of advice, one that succinctly sums up the gangster mentality built on loyalty. Ripped from Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas (based on Nicholas Pilegg's non-fiction crime chronicle Wiseguy ), De Niro’s James “Jimmy” Conway offers the following sage advice: "Never rat on your friends and always keep your mouth shut."

The line comes after a young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) refuses to talk following a bust for selling untaxed cigarettes, earning his stripes by making it through his first court appearance without informing on any of his accomplices. Outside the courtroom, Conway slips him a handful of cash and congratulates him on surviving his first pinch. Then he pulls Henry close and imparts the cardinal rules of their world, turning a low-level arrest into a defining rite of passage for a kid desperate to prove his place in the organization.
points: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro.
Across decades of mob dramas, he's played men who command respect through intimidation, calculation, and a religious devotion to the rules of their world.
Through all these roles, De Niro has delivered plenty of unforgettable lines, but one of his most memorable isn't a threat or a declaration of power.
It's a deceptively simple piece of advice, one that succinctly sums up the gangster mentality built on loyalty.

articles.title: Tenebris Somnia Blends 2D Visuals With Live-Action Horror Scenes, And It’s Already On Sale At Launch
articles.summary: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension. If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please).
body: As the best horror games continue to push for more realistic visuals and immersive experiences, Tenebris Somnia’s twist on the genre combines old-school cool with movie-like cutscenes. It’s both jarring and original, and that’s exactly what makes for excellent horror. I want to be constantly surprised, and Tenebris Somnia makes its pixelated 2D threats even more menacing when you see live-action versions of the monsters.

Co-created by Andrés Borghi and Tobías Rusjan with Saibot Studios, and published by New Blood Interactive, the studio behind Ultrakill, Blood West, and Gloomwood, Tenebris Somnia’s style is fittingly inspired by past eras of console gaming. Its pixelated visuals make the switch to live-action cutscenes even more unsettling. It’s almost like Clock Tower, but if it randomly turned into a movie at any second. No, I’m not shaking; you are.
points: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension.
If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please).

articles.title: Battlefield 6 devs to fix "Secuty" skin typo, but five-pistol outfit was intentional
articles.summary: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.
body: The studio acknowledged "candid feedback" from players in a statement on social media, insisting it had "hear[d] your concerns".

And though the statement did not mention AI - either to admit or deny using the generative tech - BattlefieldComm said that while the 'Secuty' typo will be addressed by a "correction update", an outfit with five pistols is intentional.

"First, let's dive into the 'Secuty' typo patches on the McNeil character," the studio wrote. "A correction update has already been planned for the Season 5 Phase 2 release. However, we recognise that letting a known visual error go live without quick acknowledgement creates confusion and erodes trust. We are reviewing how we communicate known visual bugs so you aren’t left wondering whether something was intentional or overlooked."

The five-pistol-touting Midnight Mirage skin, however, is described as an "intentional creative concept" and "a nod to over-the-top action movie tropes where an operative inexplicably has another backup weapon strapped to every spare inch of gear".

articles.title: 8 Mass Effect Replay Ideas That Make the Trilogy Feel Brand-New
articles.summary: Every replay of the Mass Effect games tends to start with a promise: this time, you’ll do things differently. Then Shepard makes the same speech, you bring the same squad, and you’re right back where you started.
body: The Renegade path is an uneven one in this trilogy. Your dialogue options are color-coded: You get a blue, diplomatic Paragon option and a red, ruthless Renegade one. The red options mean different things at different times. In Mass Effect 1, they swing between prejudice, efficiency, and plain rudeness. By the time you get to Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3, the Renegade options settle on one primary idea: Getting the job done at any cost. One effective approach, is to take the red option nearly every time, and go Paragon only for the choices the sequels depend upon. Be ruthless, but leave a few people alive. Like Wrex, at least. For the story’s sake.

Mass Effect 1 asks you to pick a pre-service history (Spacer, Colonist, or Earthborn) and a psychological profile (Sole Survivor, War Hero, or Ruthless). Each history and profile unlocks its own mission, like “Old Friends” for Earthborn Shepards, where a former gang member asks you for a favor.
points: Every replay of the Mass Effect games tends to start with a promise: this time, you’ll do things differently.

articles.title: Drunken Goddess Reflux Devs Cancel Steam Next Fest Demo Over AI Clone Concerns
articles.summary: Drunken Goddess Reflux is an upcoming indie game where players must survive a night of drinking with a beautiful anime demon, Russian Roulette-style. It's certainly a unique concept, and the game has already amassed over 25,000 wishlists on Steam.
body: Steam Next Fest is set to begin Monday, Oct. 19, and end Oct. 26. The purpose of this weeklong event is for developers to share demos of their upcoming games. It's a great initiative that lets players try out plenty of titles for free and helps developers publicize their games and gain wishlists on Steam.

Alliance Arts and Who You's upcoming game, Drunken Goddess Reflux, was going to release a Steam Next Fest demo on Oct. 19. However, just a few days before the event, Alliance Arts decided to pull the plug. The studio apologized to fans anticipating the demo on X, explaining that it could not move forward for two reasons.

First, it would be unable to monitor whether gameplay footage and streams would be in accordance with its publishing restrictions; second, it believed providing a demo would enable others to quickly produce clones using generative AI.

articles.summary: Leaker Kepler_L2 claims the PS6's RAM and NAND alone cost over $680. Sony has said it doesn't intend to sell hardware at significant losses.
body: The PS6's memory and storage reportedly cost more than $680 between them.

That's according to leaker Kepler_L2, who wrote that "RAM + NAND alone is over $680" in a NeoGAF thread in which Kepler_L2 was replying to a forum user who doubted an earlier cost estimate and suggested Sony could subsidise the PS6 to launch at $680.

In June, insider Kepler_L2 - who has previously made claims about hardware that have turned out to be true - claimed the console's bill of materials had climbed to close to $1,000, up from their earlier estimate of around $760.
Kepler_L2 didn't say how they arrived at the figure, and Sony has not, of course, confirmed any PS6 specs or pricing.

articles.title: Street Fighter Fails To Match Resident Evil's Opening Weekend Box Office Success
articles.summary: Looking at the fall slate of blockbuster films, I was most interested in finding out whether Resident Evil or Street Fighter would have the bigger opening weekend. We now have our answer: Street Fighter grossed about half of what Resident Evil did in its first weekend.
body: Deadline reports that Street Fighter, an adaptation of Capcom's series of fighting games, grossed $31 million its opening weekend. By comparison, the Capcom horror game adaptation Resident Evil made $60 million its opening weekend and is still charting at the box office about a month after release.

Street Fighter is opening lower than Mortal Kombat 2, another fighting game adaptation released this year, and doing worse than what you'd expect from a blockbuster movie. Ultimately, its gross ended up in line with industry pre-release expectations, though. The real overperformer of the weekend was the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything, which had the second-biggest opening for a theatrically released documentary ever at $15 million.

Street Fighter and Resident Evil took two very different approaches to adaptations. Street Fighter leaned into well-known characters, fan service, and the wackiness of the IP to draw people in. Meanwhile, Resident Evil took the essence and themes of its franchise and used them to tell a completely original story.
points: Looking at the fall slate of blockbuster films, I was most interested in finding out whether Resident Evil or Street Fighter would have the bigger opening weekend.
We now have our answer: Street Fighter grossed about half of what Resident Evil did in its first weekend.

articles.title: The Outlast Trials' initial playtests went poorly: Designer says 6-year development took 'a f**king long time' and 'a s**t-ton of prototypes'
articles.summary: Gamedev may as well be conducted in a black box as far as many players are concerned, so it can be easy to think of a good game as one where development went smoothly and a bad game as one where things went terribly awry.
body: As Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin told Gamespot in a recent interview, it took six years to turn the vague notion of a co-op Outlast game into something ready to launch via early access. It was "a fucking long time," as he recalled it, and the product of "a shit-ton of prototypes."

"[The Red Barrels team] went too far trying to make [The Outlast Trials] systemic, random, and trying to reach our ultimate goal of infinite replayability," he told Gamespot. "We needed to come back to something that maybe added less replayability, but definitely felt more like Outlast." The article notes that a seemingly shippable build was produced within four years, but playtests went poorly enough to send the team back to the drawing board.

I suppose concerns about replayability have been put to rest now that it's mutated into a sizable live service game with around 20,000 people playing as I write this, though the game's ongoing development isn't entirely free from strife—as the article points out, players are mixed on its use of AI-generated imagery, and Outlast 3 was seemingly put on the backburner after Trials proved a huge success.

articles.title: Samson dev Liquid Swords has reportedly gone bankrupt
articles.summary: Swedish studio Liquid Swords, maker of action game Samson, has reportedly been put into bankruptcy.
body: Break It (thanks, PC Gamer ) reports that the studio's almost 30 employees will be compensated by the state, and that the bankruptcy trustee is looking for a buyer.

The original report suggests Liquid Swords has not paid its developers for months, but the bankruptcy order, thought to have been issued on 12th October, should mean unpaid salaries will be covered by Sweden's state wage guarantee.
Christofer Sundberg, who co-founded Just Cause developer Avalanche Studios, set up Liquid Swords in 2020.

Samson: A Tyndalston Story, the studio's first game, launched on PC on 8th April, followed by PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on 21st September. The studio initially had difficulty securing a publisher, and reviews were ultimately mixed with players complaining of technical and performance issues.

articles.title: God of War Laufey's £130 Collector Box doesn't come with the game
articles.summary: God of War Laufey's £129.99 Collector Box has a light-up Faye statue, an Oracle Deck, and a mini artbook, but the game is sold separately.
body: God of War Laufey's Collector Box will cost £129.99 and will not include the game.
That's according to an update on the PlayStation Blog, which confirms the box, priced at $149.99 and €149.99, contains a light-up Faye statue, a 51-card Oracle Deck, and a mini artbook.
The eight-inch statue shows Faye, Phranque, and Rue taking on Begtse's soldiers, and "Phranque will light up when the statue is plugged into a USB power source" (thanks, ScreenRant ).

The Oracle Deck has custom illustrations by Megan Lara on every card, and Sony describes it as "a beautiful representation of your adventure through the Everywhen". The mini artbook collects concept art of the game's characters, creatures, and environments, "hand-selected by our talented art team at Santa Monica Studio".

articles.title: 'There were a lot of disagreements across the place': Former Marathon director Joe Ziegler on leading Bungie's extraction shooter, playing Path of Exile for 3,437 hours, and why he'll never uninstall Kingdom Hearts
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Joe Ziegler might be best known for his role guiding the design of big competitive shooters, but his formative gaming experiences were with point-and-click adventures like King's Quest. "There was something so clever about trying to use all this knowledge about random things like fairy tales to try to solve puzzles inside of the game," he says. "It was just that 'A-ha!' moment where videogames could be these really engaging ways for you to be clever and creative."

Ziegler started out at Pandemic Studios, where he worked as a mission designer on 2009's The Saboteur. But he is best known as game director on Riot's hugely popular arena shooter Valorant, and his more recent oversight of Bungie's extraction-shooter revival of Marathon, which he assumed leadership of in March 2024 following the dismissal of former director Christopher Barret.

articles.title: Clive Barker says he's 'genuinely astonished' by Hellraiser: Revival: 'I'm proud as f**k at the end result'
articles.summary: Hellraiser: Revival's commitment to being both gnarly and horny has already been thoroughly documented, with PC Gamer's Wes Fenlon describing it as " nasty nasty" in his preview.
body: In an interview with horror site Dread Central (via FRVR ), Barker admitted that he had concerns about the project going into it, but was thoroughly impressed by the final product. "I'm proud as f**k at the end result," he said. "I was fearful at one point that the game would be overly censored, but I'm genuinely astonished by how far they've been able to push it."

Barker, who worked closely with developer Saber Interactive to shape Revival's world and to advise on the game's story, reckons that Saber Interactive's work on the game is a prime example of how to approach adapting a license. "I think what was achieved in the game is a wake-up call to anyone who's been involved in the making of a franchise like Hellraiser," the author and director explained.

articles.title: Frozen Trail finally puts the 'raid' in Arc Raiders
articles.summary: The Fallen Emperor and Arc Frigate have me excited for the game's future.
body: I'm standing on top of a flying fortress hundreds of feet in the air, as around me, 15 or so players wage a losing battle against a swarm of flying robots armed with rockets and lasers. It's utter chaos. We fight further and further into the ship, unlocking platforms, defeating waves of enemies and giant turrets which pop out of the deck to gun down unsuspecting looters. But I think we're done.

Time is running short and we've once again stalled at this stage of the puzzle. All that's left now is to try and make it back to ground in one piece and live to attempt another day. This is the Frigate, one of Arc Raiders two new raid-style activities, and it's exactly what the game needed.

Rather than content you can complete the day the update comes out, Frozen Trail 's Frigate and Fallen Emperor represent a deeper loot chase, tied into upgrading the new outpost and workbenches to fashion special weapons which fire explosive bullets or incendiary grenades.
points: The Fallen Emperor and Arc Frigate have me excited for the game's future.

videos.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Overview Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time game launches November 5, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2 system. Pre-orders are available now: ninten.do/6016asy0M
body: The story of Link’s adventure and growth transcends time in this classic tale, built from the ground up for Nintendo Switch 2. As you venture through the Kingdom of Hyrule, you’ll meet lively characters, battle ferocious monsters, and solve puzzles scattered throughout dungeons. Use all sorts of items, including the titular ocarina, to suit your needs and forge a path forward.

This title will support ZELDA NOTES, a game-specific service usable with the Nintendo Switch App for smart devices. Two new amiibo figures are also on the way; tap them to receive special in-game masks. And by tapping amiibo of characters from the Legend of Zelda games, you can get in-game items that may help you on your journey.
